packageRules.description: Skip FlakeHub inputs: Renovate's nix manager only supports the git-refs datasource (git ls-remote), and flakehub.com is HTTP-only (tarball + REST API), so it can never resolve. Transitive deps that point to FlakeHub will still update.

Group every update by the directory its package file lives in, so each project folder (helm chart, Go module, Python project, nix flake, etc.) gets a single PR. A folder holding multiple ecosystems (e.g. cmd/lab has go.mod + flake.nix) is grouped together because they share the same packageFileDir. separateMajorMinor (default) still splits majors into their own PR.
Root-level nix flake inputs have an empty packageFileDir; give them an explicit group name.
Don't apply minimumReleaseAge to jellyfin image+appVersion so they stay grouped

LinuxServer images: strip the -ls build suffix so Renovate matches the UPSTREAM project's release tags (via each image's sourceUrl override below) and renders its changelog. Trade-off: because the -ls revision is dropped from version comparison, LinuxServer-only rebuilds at the same upstream version no longer generate PRs.

qBittorrent (LinuxServer) uses <qbt>_v<libtorrent>-ls<n> tags on the libtorrent-2.x main track (the separate libtorrentv1-... track is excluded by the leading-digit anchor). Track only the qBittorrent version: this overrides the generic LinuxServer extractVersion/versioning above and matches qBittorrent's release-X.Y.Z upstream tags via Renovate's built-in 'release' changelog keyword. Same trade-off as the other LinuxServer images: libtorrent-only or ls-only rebuilds at the same qBittorrent version won't generate PRs.
Forgejo releases on codeberg link out to a separate release-notes markdown doc instead of inlining notes; point changelogUrl at that doc directly.

The dagger SDK's own dependencies are owned by `dagger develop`, which rewrites them to whatever the pinned CLI wants. `dagger develop` runs as a post-upgrade task, which would overwrite renovate's changest to these packages.

Tidy go.mod/go.sum and apply golangci-lint autofixes after any gomod update, for Go modules that need no other generated artifact. cmd/lab (nix vendorHash) and .dagger (SDK codegen via `dagger develop`) have their own rules below with extra steps beyond lint-go, so they're excluded here — matchFileNames uses negative patterns rather than rule ordering because postUpgradeTasks isn't a mergeable config option: if two matching packageRules both set it, the later match fully replaces the earlier one's commands rather than combining them. Without this rule, a bumped dependency can leave go.sum untidy (extra/stale checksum lines) and fail the `dagger check` gomod-tidy gate, blocking automerge — this is how secret-sync's go.sum went untidy in the first place. lint-go operates on every discovered Go module in the repo, not just the one that triggered it (same as the other `dagger generate` rules below), so fileFilters isn't scoped to a single directory.

Recompute the nix buildGoModule vendorHash after anything under cmd/lab changes. Renovate rewrites go.mod/go.sum which breaks the nix package. lint-go runs first (tidying go.mod/go.sum and applying any golangci-lint autofixes a dependency bump requires, e.g. import changes) so the vendor hash is computed from the final, tidy go.mod/go.sum rather than Renovate's raw edit. lint-go also touches every other Go module in the repo, hence the broad fileFilters alongside cmd/lab/** (needed for gomod.json, which holds the vendor hash).

Regenerate dagger's own artifacts after any update inside .dagger. `dagger develop` handles the generated SDK bindings (dagger.gen.go, internal/**) and runs first so codegen matches the new dependency version. lint-go (mod tidy + golangci-lint --fix, which supersedes format-go since --fix also applies formatter fixes) then tidies and lints every Go module in the repo, not just .dagger, since a Go toolchain or golangci-lint bump can affect all of them. The remaining `dagger generate` targets handle non-Go source regenerated by other tooling updates, e.g. when an updated cue formats files differently than the previous version.
